Genes, Populations, & Evolution
¨Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium:
¤Required conditions are rarely (if ever) met
¤Deviations from a Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium indicate that evolution has taken place
¤Analysis of allele changes in populations over time determines the extent to which evolution has occurred.
explanation: Because the conditions necessary for Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium are rarely, if ever, met in nature, real populations typically deviate from equilibrium. Any observed deviation from HWE indicates that evolution has taken place. By analyzing these shifts and changes in allele frequencies over time, population geneticists can determine the direction and extent of evolutionary change within a population.

questions.q: What does a deviation from Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium indicate about a population?
questions.exp: A deviation from Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium indicates that allele frequencies have shifted, which means that evolution has occurred.
